truth_states: FACT = source-derived at the cited line; UPSTREAM = in-tree doc claim (drift-prone); INFERENCE = producer reasoning, labeled in place; AUTHORITY = HX governance decision

entries.name: central-authz-pipeline-next16-proxy-convention
entries.purpose: Next.js 16's renamed middleware convention (src/proxy.ts, matcher at src/proxy.ts:35-52 covering /, /dashboard/*, /home*, /api/*, case-insensitive /v1*, /v1beta*, /chat/*, /responses*, /codex*, /models) runs runAuthzPipeline(request, {enforce:true}) on every matched request: classification, trusted-header strip, body-size check, OPTIONS preflight, IP filter, policy evaluation, CSRF/Origin check, subject stamping. [FACT] Cross-ref CAP-P1-902: P1 correctly found no middleware.ts, but the Next-16 proxy.ts convention DOES provide a central interception layer in addition to per-route defense-in-depth — the sibling entry's 'per-route interception confirmed' conclusion is refined here.
entries.risk_class: critical — this is the single chokepoint authenticating and classifying every dashboard/API request; a matcher gap (as in GHSA-jvqc-mp9f-q936's case-sensitivity miss) silently bypasses all central authZ
entries.test_contract: Routed: request each route class and assert stamped x-omniroute-route-class; negative: unauthenticated management request → 401 JSON, uppercase /V1/ alias still classified CLIENT_API (GHSA-jvqc-mp9f-q936 regression); matcher-diff test against next.config.mjs rewrites
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove/rename src/proxy.ts (Next stops running it — catastrophic, authZ becomes per-route only); no supported disable flag exists

entries.name: route-classification-public-clientapi-management
entries.purpose: classifyRoute normalizes the path (trailing slash, case-insensitive client-API control segments per GHSA-jvqc-mp9f-q936, /codex→/api/v1/responses and /v1/v1 double-prefix aliases) and assigns exactly one of PUBLIC / CLIENT_API / MANAGEMENT, with anything unmatched falling back to MANAGEMENT (fail-closed). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — every downstream gate keys on this classification; an alias/normalization miss reclasses a client route as management or vice versa
dependencies: next.config.mjs rewrite aliases (must stay in sync, per src/proxy.ts:33-34 comment)
entries.test_contract: Unit: exhaustive path matrix incl. case variants and trailing slashes; negative: unknown path classifies MANAGEMENT not PUBLIC
entries.rollback_or_disable: None (pure function); revert = code change

entries.name: public-route-classification-constants-shape-split
entries.purpose: The public (no-dashboard-auth) API surface is defined here as data: 6 genuine subtree PREFIXES (must end in '/'), an EXACT single-route set, 3 read-only routes that also get CORS relaxation, '/api/health' exact read-only without CORS relaxation, 3 method-scoped cloud routes, and a LOCAL_ONLY exclusion list for OAuth auto-import routes (GHSA-wgwc-crjm-pmwv / GHSA-gxv4-955v-v6cm); shape-split after GHSA-74g9-q8f6-793h because startsWith prefix matching shadowed /api/usage/[connectionId]. [FACT] Cross-ref CAP-P1 (flagged critical there).
entries.risk_class: critical — one wrong line silently de-gates a management route (the GHSA-74g9 incident class); the file's own header documents 11 near-miss entries
entries.test_contract: Unit: every prefix asserted trailing-slash; negative: adjacent dynamic routes (/api/usage/<id>) classify MANAGEMENT; regression: GHSA-74g9 shadow case
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the offending entry from the relevant set; routes fall back to MANAGEMENT classification

entries.name: central-management-policy-ordered-gates
entries.purpose: managementPolicy.evaluate is the authoritative management gate, ordered: ws-bridge secret → Tier-1 LOCAL_ONLY loopback/LAN gate (with manage-scope/dashboard bypass) → inspector-ingest/model-sync/video-bridge/internal-service self-hop tokens → loopback CLI machine token → /api/mcp/ mcp:connect carve-out (#9159) → requireLogin=false anonymous bypass (skipped for ALWAYS_PROTECTED) → dashboard JWT session → oma_ access token (scope-checked) → manage-scope API key → reject 401/403 (503 on auth-backend failure). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: critical — gate-ordering or fail-open regression here defeats every authenticator below the fault; it deliberately degrades closed (503) on DB errors
entries.test_contract: Policy unit matrix per gate; negative: forged peer-stamp, URL-borne key (#3300), wrong-scope oma_ → 403; auth-backend throw → 503 not 403
entries.rollback_or_disable: None; central policy has no feature flag (requireLogin=false is the only sanctioned relaxation and ALWAYS_PROTECTED survives it)

entries.name: route-level-requiremanagementauth-defense-in-depth
entries.purpose: Per-route management guard re-checking auth inside handlers (dashboard session → trusted loopback internal service → stamped local-cli subject → CLI token → oma_ token → manage-scope API key, header-only per #3300); measured usage: 286 route.ts files across 56 top-level /api domains (grep -rln over src/app/api). [FACT] Cross-ref P1's '~100 management domains': 56 of 102 top-level domains call this guard directly; the rest rely on the central policy, public classification, or their own auth.
entries.risk_class: high — it is the second line if the proxy matcher ever misses a path, but it does NOT re-enforce the LOCAL_ONLY tier (central-policy-only), so spawn-capable routes depend on src/proxy.ts running
entries.test_contract: Route-level negative tests per handler (no credential → 401; valid inference-only key → 403 manage-scope message); divergence test: routes calling it vs central classification
entries.rollback_or_disable: Returns null (allow) when isAuthRequired() is false — disabled globally by requireLogin=false except ALWAYS_PROTECTED paths (central tier)

entries.name: dashboard-session-jwt-authn
entries.purpose: Dashboard authN is an HS256 JWT in the httpOnly auth_token cookie (30d expiry, sameSite=lax, secure gated by AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE or forwarded-proto https at pipeline.ts:136-143), verified with jose against process.env.JWT_SECRET — no JWT_SECRET means session auth is unconditionally false (fail-closed, apiAuth.ts:222); the pipeline auto-refreshes tokens inside a 7-day window and drops stale cookies on signature failure. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — the JWT_SECRET signs all dashboard sessions; it is auto-generated and persisted in plaintext in SQLite (see CAP-P4-039), so DB-file read access equals session-forgery capability
entries.test_contract: Direct: login sets cookie, /api/auth/status reflects session; negative: tampered JWT → 401, missing JWT_SECRET → login 500 + session check false
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unset JWT_SECRET and delete the persisted 'jwtSecret' row → all sessions invalid; requireLogin=false disables the requirement (except ALWAYS_PROTECTED)

entries.name: management-password-bcrypt-changeme-bootstrap
entries.purpose: The dashboard management password is stored as bcrypt (12 rounds, managementPassword.ts:5) and verified with bcrypt.compare; .env.example ships INITIAL_PASSWORD=CHANGEME as a bootstrap placeholder, and the module logs a loud '[AUTH][SECURITY]' warning while the well-known default remains set (managementPassword.ts:79-81). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — an operator who skips first-boot hardening runs a dashboard reachable with the published default password; bcrypt+warning mitigate but cannot enforce rotation
dependencies: INITIAL_PASSWORD or onboarding wizard for first set
entries.test_contract: Direct: login with configured password succeeds; negative: CHANGEME rejected after a real password is set; boot log asserts warning present while default active
entries.rollback_or_disable: Change password via Dashboard → Settings → Security (writes bcrypt hash); remove INITIAL_PASSWORD from env

entries.name: login-bruteforce-guard
entries.purpose: Per-client-IP sliding-window lockout for /api/auth/login: 5 failures within 15 min → 15 min lockout with retryAfter, in-process Map with a 256-entry opportunistic prune so distributed brute force cannot grow it unboundedly; keyed on the trusted stamped peer IP when available, toggleable via the bruteForceProtection setting (default true). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — single-process memory scope by design (its header states it pairs with reverse-proxy rate limiting), so a multi-replica deploy would get per-replica budgets
dependencies: trusted peer IP stamp (CAP-P4-019) for a non-spoofable key
entries.test_contract: Negative: 5 bad logins → 429-style rejection with retryAfterSeconds; success clears attempts; prune leaves guard decisions unchanged
entries.rollback_or_disable: bruteForceProtection setting false → guard is a no-op (checkLoginGuard/recordLoginFailure early-return)

entries.name: client-api-authn-policy-require-api-key
entries.purpose: CLIENT_API (/v1*, /v1beta*, aliases) authenticates via Bearer, x-api-key, x-goog-api-key (#7034), or path-scoped URL token (extractBearer falls through non-Bearer Authorization rather than rejecting); REQUIRE_API_KEY=false (.env.example default) allows anonymous inference, and with it false an INVALID bearer degrades to anonymous with a warning instead of 401 (#2257); a WS-descriptor handshake GET is pre-authorized anonymous (clientApi.ts:10-19, 65-67). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — on the HX LAN the default REQUIRE_API_KEY=false means any LAN host can spend provider quota through the proxy unauthenticated; the invalid-key-degrades-to-anonymous path removes the signal a typo'd key would otherwise give
entries.test_contract: Direct: valid key → 200; negative: REQUIRE_API_KEY=true + no key → 401 AUTH_002, invalid key → 401; flag-off: anonymous allowed and bad key falls through with warning
entries.rollback_or_disable: REQUIRE_API_KEY=false (default) — the disable mechanism itself; per-key revocation in the API Keys dashboard

entries.name: scoped-cli-access-tokens-oma-remote-mode
entries.purpose: Remote-mode CLI access uses oma_-prefixed bearer tokens verified against the DB (unknown/expired/revoked → 401, DB throw → 503), with the required scope inferred per request; the public exact route /api/cli/connect bootstraps a token by exchanging the management password (its handler enforces password check + lockout). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — oma_ tokens are management credentials; scope inference is method/prefix-based, so a prefix-list mistake grants write or admin to a read token
entries.test_contract: Direct: read token GETs management route; negative: read token POSTs → 403 insufficient-scope naming have/need; revoked token → 401
entries.rollback_or_disable: Revoke the token row (verifyAccessToken fails → 401); tokens are per-name revocable in the CLI tokens surface

entries.name: local-cli-machine-token-loopback-only
entries.purpose: The local CLI authenticates with an HMAC-SHA256 token derived from the host machine-id (salt OMNIROUTE_CLI_SALT or builtin), accepted only from verified loopback (trusted locality stamp, never the Host header) and compared timing-safe; OMNIROUTE_DISABLE_CLI_TOKEN=true kills the path; the raw header is stripped before handlers (pipeline.ts:350). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — machine-id-derived tokens are guessable to anyone with host-level knowledge of the machine-id and salt; the loopback requirement is the real control, so it must never trust a spoofable locality signal
entries.test_contract: Direct: local CLI call with token succeeds; negative: same token from non-loopback locality → rejected; OMNIROUTE_DISABLE_CLI_TOKEN=true → rejected even on loopback
entries.rollback_or_disable: OMNIROUTE_DISABLE_CLI_TOKEN=true env

entries.name: internal-service-and-selfhop-token-carveouts
entries.purpose: A family of narrow, exact-path internal authenticators lets OmniRoute's own components through the management gate: internal-service token (env or file, timing-safe, loopback+stamped locality required in requireManagementAuth's variant), codex WS-bridge per-process secret (management.ts:103-121), loopback inspector-ingest token (:238-244), internal model-sync (:246-248), and video-bridge broker/drill-down per-process tokens (:254-265). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — each carve-out is a standing management-auth bypass keyed on a shared secret; they are exact-path and loopback-scoped by design, and any widening recreates the RCE-via-tunnel class
entries.test_contract: Negative per carve-out: wrong/absent secret → falls through to standard auth and rejects; non-loopback peer → LOCAL_ONLY 403 before the carve-out
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unset the corresponding env secret — every validator early-returns false when unconfigured

entries.name: oidc-dashboard-sso
entries.purpose: Optional OIDC SSO for the dashboard: isAuthRequired treats oidcEnabled+issuer+clientId+clientSecret as a configured authenticator alongside the password, and the /api/auth/oidc/ prefix is PUBLIC-classified so login/callback handlers can run unauthenticated (login route GET handler at the cited line). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — a second dashboard authN path whose client secret lives in settings; misconfiguration locks or exposes the dashboard, but it is disabled unless fully configured
entries.test_contract: Direct: OIDC login redirect issued when configured; negative: unconfigured → routes inert; callback with bad state → rejected (handler-level, not verified this partition)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Set oidcEnabled=false / clear the OIDC settings — isAuthRequired stops counting it

entries.name: local-only-tier-spawn-capable-routes
entries.purpose: Tier-1 route guard: 43 measured prefix entries + 4 regex patterns (/api/providers/{id}/login, volcengine-plan connect, refresh-cursor, chatgpt-web-codex-doctor) listing every child-process-spawning or host-credential-reading route (/api/mcp/, /api/services/, /api/plugins/, /api/settings/mitm, /api/tunnels/*, /api/cli-tools/*-settings, /api/system/version, /api/db-backups/exportAll, /api/jobs, /api/acp/agents, OAuth auto-imports, etc.) — blocked unconditionally for non-loopback/non-private-LAN peers (GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj class), with two GET-only exemptions (/api/system/version, /api/tunnels/cloudflared status). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: critical — this is the control standing between a leaked dashboard credential/tunnel and remote process spawn on the OmniRoute host; membership gaps are RCE
entries.test_contract: Negative matrix: every prefix from a remote-stamped peer → 403 LOCAL_ONLY; check-route-guard-membership script re-derives membership; GET-exemption exact-match only
entries.rollback_or_disable: None (no flag); private-LAN widening is the sanctioned relaxation (owner-authorized upstream 2026-05-30, routeGuard.ts:190-195)

entries.name: manage-scope-local-only-bypass-with-killswitch
entries.purpose: Opt-in escape hatch: DB-stored bypass prefixes (compile-time default just /api/mcp/) become reachable from non-loopback when the caller holds a manage/admin-scope API key (or mcp:connect for /api/mcp/, #7895) or a dashboard session; the runtime decision reads a hot-reloaded snapshot, refuses any prefix that is a parent/child of a spawn-capable prefix (defense-in-depth beyond the zod schema), and is globally killable via localOnlyManageScopeBypassEnabled. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: critical — it deliberately pokes authenticated holes in the Tier-1 spawn guard; a crafted bypass prefix row is the exact failure the parent/child spawn-prefix rejection exists to catch
dependencies: manage-scope API key or dashboard session
entries.test_contract: Negative: bypass prefix '/api/cli-tools/' never grants /api/cli-tools/runtime/*; unauthenticated request to bypassable path → 403; kill-switch off → all bypasses inert
entries.rollback_or_disable: localOnlyManageScopeBypassEnabled=false setting; or empty the DB bypass prefix list

entries.name: always-protected-tier-credential-dump-routes
entries.purpose: Tier-2: six paths (/api/shutdown, /api/providers/health-autopilot/actions, /api/settings/database, /api/db-backups, /api/settings/export-json, /api/settings/import-json) stay authenticated even when requireLogin=false, because they are credential dumps or irreversible replacements (GHSA-mghq-58h3-qcqj, GHSA-v7g9-7f55-5g46). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: critical — these routes export or replace the entire credential store; the tier exists because their handlers once trusted isAuthRequired() alone
dependencies: management policy Tier-2 check ordering (before the anonymous bypass)
entries.test_contract: Negative: with requireLogin=false, each path still 401s anonymous callers; boundary-match test (/api/db-backups* covered, lookalikes not)
entries.rollback_or_disable: None (that is the point); membership changes are source edits

entries.name: access-token-scope-inference-policy
entries.purpose: Required-scope inference for oma_ tokens (owner-confirmed upstream policy 2026-06-19): GET/HEAD/OPTIONS → read, mutations → write, except 6 admin-for-all-methods prefixes (/api/cli/tokens, /api/oauth, /api/auth, /api/policy, /api/services, /api/mcp) and 2 admin-on-mutation prefixes (/api/providers, /api/cli-tools/apply); prefix matching is exact-or-segment-boundary to avoid lookalike over-match (/api/auth vs /api/authz-inventory). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — a new sensitive route defaults to write-not-admin by design, so the admin lists are a manual sensitivity registry that can silently lag the route tree
entries.test_contract: Unit: pure-function matrix over methods×paths incl. segment-boundary lookalikes; governance: new-route review checks prefix-list membership
entries.rollback_or_disable: None; narrower tokens are the mitigation (issue read-only tokens)

entries.name: browser-mutation-origin-and-csrf-defense
entries.purpose: For MANAGEMENT routes authenticated by dashboard cookie, unsafe methods must pass validateBrowserMutationOrigin (Fetch Metadata + Origin against configured/public candidates) or present a valid dashboard CSRF token — an HMAC-SHA256 over context+expiry+session-hash keyed by JWT_SECRET, 10-minute TTL, timing-safe compared; failure → 403 INVALID_ORIGIN. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — this is the CSRF control for the cookie-authenticated management plane; CORS being fail-closed is not sufficient alone because simple-form posts don't preflight
entries.test_contract: Negative: cross-site POST with cookie but no valid Origin/token → 403; token forgery/expiry → invalid; same-origin dashboard write passes
entries.rollback_or_disable: None; bearer-key clients are unaffected (check applies only to dashboard_session subjects)

entries.name: peer-stamp-token-locality-trust
entries.purpose: The custom Node server stamps the real TCP peer IP and a via-proxy marker as <token>|<payload> headers; the pipeline timing-safe validates them against the per-process OMNIROUTE_PEER_STAMP_TOKEN and derives the sole trustworthy locality verdict (loopback/lan/remote — fail-closed to remote when absent/forged), downgrading any loopback/LAN socket to remote when forwarding headers were present (the decolua/9router da667836 reverse-proxy bypass class). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: critical — every loopback/LAN-gated control (Tier-1 spawn guard, CLI token, internal tokens) inherits its strength; when the stamp token is unset, locality fails closed to remote and local-only surfaces break rather than open
entries.test_contract: Negative: forged stamp → remote verdict; via-proxy stamped request with loopback socket → remote; direct loopback with valid stamp → loopback
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unset OMNIROUTE_PEER_STAMP_TOKEN → all locality remote (fail-closed degradation, local CLI flows stop)

entries.name: operator-ip-filter-blacklist-whitelist
entries.purpose: Operator-configured IP blacklist/whitelist with priority modes and ephemeral temp bans, enforced in the pipeline for non-loopback peers using the trusted stamped peer IP (not spoofable forwarding headers — #9033 D1), persisted to key_value namespace 'ipFilter' so restarts keep the policy (#6131); loopback is exempt so the operator cannot lock themselves out. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — disabled by default and defense-in-depth only; on HX it is the closest in-app equivalent of a network ACL, since no host firewall exists [AUTHORITY: owner rule 2026-08-26]
dependencies: dashboard settings writer (separate module instance, hot-propagated per D2)
entries.test_contract: Negative: blacklisted stamped peer → 403; loopback always allowed; whitelist mode denies non-listed; persistence survives reload
entries.rollback_or_disable: Disable toggle in settings (enabled=false → checkRequestIP no-op); clear lists

entries.name: request-body-size-guard
entries.purpose: Pre-parse body-size rejection in the pipeline for non-GET/OPTIONS /api/* requests: default 10 MB (MAX_BODY_SIZE_BYTES), with route-class exceptions (import/audio 100 MB, files 500 MB, LLM API 50 MB, media uncapped by design so provider limits decide). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — OOM/DoS control on the hot path; the uncapped media class is a deliberate residual exposure
entries.test_contract: Negative: oversized body → rejection before handler; boundary: exactly-at-limit passes; per-class limit table asserted
entries.rollback_or_disable: MAX_BODY_SIZE_BYTES env raises the default; no full disable found (media class excepted by design)

entries.name: prompt-injection-guardrail-facade
entries.purpose: The chat-path prompt-injection guard is a legacy-named facade delegating to the guardrail system (evaluatePromptInjection) with per-guardrail disable resolution via resolveDisabledGuardrails; wired into /v1/chat/completions admission (cross-ref CAP-P1-003). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — a content heuristics layer, not an auth boundary; its value is operator visibility and optional blocking of injection-shaped prompts
entries.test_contract: Direct: injection-shaped body flagged/blocked per policy; negative: disabled guardrail id → pass-through
entries.rollback_or_disable: Per-guardrail disable via resolveDisabledGuardrails settings

entries.name: management-api-key-scopes-model
entries.purpose: Single source of truth for management scopes: manage and admin (admin is a superset) authorize API keys on management routes; mcp:connect is a deliberately narrow additive scope granting only the /api/mcp/ LOCAL_ONLY carve-out, kept out of MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_SCOPES so it never widens general management access. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — scope-set membership is the authorization decision for every key-authenticated management call; editing this file is an authZ policy change
entries.test_contract: Unit: hasManageScope/hasMcpConnectOrManageScope truth tables; negative: inference-only scopes rejected on management routes
entries.rollback_or_disable: None; scopes are per-key data — revoke or re-scope the key

entries.name: trusted-header-strip-and-subject-stamping
entries.purpose: The pipeline deletes all x-omniroute-* trusted headers (route class, auth kind/id/label/scopes, peer locality, trusted peer IP) from incoming requests before classification, then re-stamps the authenticated subject for handlers; assertAuth lets a handler verify the pipeline ran and the route class matches, throwing 401/500 on anonymous or mismatched subjects. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — if the strip list and the stamp set ever diverge, a client can pre-populate a privileged subject header and impersonate (the exact attack the headers.ts:10-12 comment names)
entries.test_contract: Negative: inbound forged x-omniroute-auth-kind → stripped, assertAuth sees anonymous; unit: every stamped header present in the strip list
entries.rollback_or_disable: None; assertAuth is opt-in per handler (defense-in-depth, not the primary gate)

entries.name: central-cors-origin-allowlist-fail-closed
entries.purpose: CORS origin decisions are centralized: no wildcard default; the Origin must match CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS / legacy CORS_ORIGIN / runtime settings list (normalized, case-insensitive) or CORS_ALLOW_ALL=true must be set — otherwise no Access-Control-Allow-Origin is emitted (fail-closed); the allowlist state is exposed to the dashboard via getCorsStatus for wildcard warnings. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — the cookie-authenticated dashboard's cross-origin protection depends on this staying fail-closed; CORS_ALLOW_ALL=true plus cookie auth would be a live-credential CSRF-read misconfiguration
dependencies: pipeline applyCorsHeaders on every response incl. rejections
entries.test_contract: Negative: unmatched Origin → no ACAO header; allowlisted Origin echoed with Vary; CORS_ALLOW_ALL echoes Origin or '*'
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unset CORS_ALLOW_ALL / remove origins from env or settings — returns to fail-closed

entries.name: token-surface-cors-origin-relaxation
entries.purpose: CLIENT_API and read-only PUBLIC routes get a permissive origin fallback (echo Origin or '*') ONLY when the request carries a credential (Authorization/x-api-key/x-goog-api-key header, auth_token cookie) or is a preflight — GHSA-7px7-29v2-m97p closed the anonymous keyless-install case where echoing an uncredentialed Origin let any web page read the API; never paired with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials; also stamps Vary: Accept-Encoding (#6737). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — the relaxation is credentialed-only and credential-header-gated by construction; the risk is a future refactor re-widening it to anonymous requests
entries.test_contract: Negative: credential-less cross-origin GET on /v1/models (keyless install) → no ACAO; token request → Origin echoed; preflight always relaxed, real request re-checked
entries.rollback_or_disable: None as a flag; classification change (route out of CLIENT_API/public_readonly) removes the relaxation

entries.name: per-route-static-cors-headers-and-preflight
entries.purpose: Route handlers spread static CORS_HEADERS (methods + allowed headers incl. anthropic-version, lease headers) and may answer OPTIONS with a 204 via handleCorsOptions; Access-Control-Allow-Origin is deliberately absent here — the central layer overlays it, so per-route code cannot reintroduce wildcard origins. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — static header values with origin control removed; residual risk is allowed-header drift between the two copies (src vs open-sse lists differ: lease headers)
entries.test_contract: Direct: OPTIONS returns 204 with methods/headers; consistency check of the two CORS_HEADERS copies
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the spread from a route; central layer still applies methods/headers

entries.name: security-response-headers-csp-xfo
entries.purpose: next.config.mjs sets a Content-Security-Policy (connect-src limited to self/loopback/https/ws, worker-src blob, manifest-src self), X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin; the API surface keeps frame-ancestors 'none' + XFO while HTML pages get frame-ancestors 'self' vscode-webview: and no XFO (:420-437) so VS Code webviews can embed. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — clickjacking/MIME-sniffing hardening; the vscode-webview frame-ancestors exception is a deliberate embed surface to keep narrow
dependencies: Next headers() config application per route group
entries.test_contract: Direct: response header assertion per surface (API vs HTML); negative: API route lacks frame-ancestors relaxation
entries.rollback_or_disable: Edit next.config.mjs headers; rebuild required

entries.name: outbound-url-guard-ssrf-core
entries.purpose: SSRF core: parseOutboundUrl allows only http/https and rejects URLs with embedded credentials; isCloudMetadataHost blocks IMDS/link-local targets (169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal/.goog, 100.100.100.200, fd00:ec2::254, all of 169.254.0.0/16, incl. IPv4-mapped IPv6 spellings) unconditionally even when private targets are opted in; parseAndValidatePublicUrl additionally blocks private hosts via the pure-JS isPrivateHost classification (loopback, RFC1918, CGNAT 100.64/10, ULA, link-local, .local/.internal/.localhost, ::ffff:*). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: critical — this guards the SSRF→IAM-credential pivot on every operator-supplied outbound URL; the checks are hostname-string based with no DNS resolution at this layer (see CAP-P4-901)
dependencies: privateHost.ts classification (browser-bundle-safe, node:net-free, parity-tested against node:net per its :15-18 comment)
entries.test_contract: Unit: metadata/link-local/mapped-IPv6 blocked in every mode; embedded userinfo rejected; private-host matrix per mode
entries.rollback_or_disable: OMNIROUTE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS=true opts out of private blocking (never metadata); legacy OUTBOUND_SSRF_GUARD_ENABLED=false implies the same

entries.name: outbound-guard-policy-modes-local-first
entries.purpose: Policy layer resolving guard mode with DB-toggle-over-env precedence: explicit private opt-in → 'none'; local-first default (OMNIROUTE_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDER_URLS, default ON) → 'block-metadata' (LAN/loopback provider endpoints validate, IMDS stays blocked); otherwise → 'public-only'; separate resolvers for the provider outbound path and the validation path (mirrored precedence, #9123). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — the default ON local mode deliberately permits LAN egress targets (correct for HX's LAN provider design), so the only universal SSRF protection left is the metadata block
entries.test_contract: Unit: mode resolution per flag combination; negative: metadata blocked under 'none'; DB toggle overrides boot-time env (Electron #2575 case)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Set OMNIROUTE_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDER_URLS=false (DB or env) → strict public-only; set private flag → no checks

entries.name: provider-node-baseurl-validation-enforcement
entries.purpose: The provider-nodes management API enforces the guard on operator-supplied baseUrl values at write time: mode none → protocol/credential parse only; block-metadata → non-metadata validation; public-only → full public validation; violations return a 400 field error, not a stored bad endpoint. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — this is where an operator (or a compromised management session) would register an SSRF target as a provider; validation is at registration, not per-request
entries.test_contract: Negative: register node with IMDS URL → 400 in all modes; LAN URL accepted in default mode; invalid protocol rejected
entries.rollback_or_disable: Guard follows the policy flags (CAP-P4-030); no separate toggle

entries.name: webhook-url-guard-wiring
entries.purpose: Webhook targets are validated by parseAndValidateWebhookUrl — protocol + embedded-credential checks unconditional, metadata/link-local blocked always, private hosts blocked unless the private opt-in is set (default OFF, #3269) — and the guard is wired at creation (zod superRefine), update, test, the validate-url helper endpoint, and at dispatch time in webhookDispatcher (defense against post-validation edits). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — webhooks carry event payloads to operator URLs; dispatch-time re-validation closes the TOCTOU between write and fire, though redirect targets are not re-validated (CAP-P4-903)
entries.test_contract: Negative: create webhook to 169.254.169.254 → rejected; private URL rejected by default, accepted with opt-in; dispatch to edited bad URL blocked
entries.rollback_or_disable: OMNIROUTE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS=true permits private targets (metadata still blocked)

entries.name: proxy-subscription-fetch-guard
entries.purpose: Server-side proxy-subscription fetching is guarded: http/https only, IMDS/link-local/0.0.0.0 blocked unconditionally, IPv4-mapped IPv6 unwrapped and re-checked (#10416), full fe80::/10 link-local coverage, and hostname resolution re-checked at fetch time so a name resolving to an internal address is refused; local/private sources are allowed by default (allowLocal:true, #10158) matching the local-first provider policy. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — subscription content is operator-supplied config fetched server-side; the fetch-time DNS re-check is the strongest anti-rebinding control in the corpus and is unique to this path
entries.test_contract: Negative: mapped-IPv6 IMDS spelling refused; hostname resolving to private IP refused at fetch; allowLocal:false restores public-only
entries.rollback_or_disable: Caller passes { allowLocal: false } for strict behavior

entries.name: openapi-try-it-proxy-auth-and-same-origin
entries.purpose: The dashboard 'Try It' proxy is management-auth gated (requireManagementAuth at handler entry — RESOLVES the CAP-P1-013 honesty flag: gating VERIFIED present), restricts targets to same-origin paths under /api/, /v1/, /v1beta/, /a2a, /.well-known/agent.json with an explicit origin equality check, strips hop-by-hop and forwarding headers, and forwards the caller's dashboard cookie. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — an authenticated server-side request forwarder riding the operator's session; the prefix allowlist and same-origin check are what keep it from being an authenticated SSRF primitive
entries.test_contract: Negative: unauthenticated → 401; path outside allowlist → 400; '//evil' scheme-relative → rejected; cross-origin target → 400
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the route file; dashboard Try-It feature dies, API unaffected

entries.name: default-executor-fallback-credential-leak-guard
entries.purpose: Cross-ref CAP-P2-004 (#6699/#10274): getExecutor hard-400s cloud-agent-only providers (jules set) and every search provider (set derived from SEARCH_PROVIDERS so a new search provider fails the regression test automatically) before DefaultExecutor's PROVIDERS.openai fallback can send the user's real provider key to OpenAI's endpoint; the fallback itself still exists for unguarded providers. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: critical — the failure class is silent credential exfiltration to a third party by design of a fallback; the guard covers two enumerated classes, and any future registry-only provider type without a guard repeats it
entries.test_contract: Negative: chat completion to jules / any search provider → 400 naming the correct surface; regression: adding a search provider without guard update fails tests (per its :232-241 comment)
entries.rollback_or_disable: None; protection is structural. The residual openai fallback has no kill switch found

entries.name: egress-proxy-assignment-fail-closed-guard
entries.purpose: When proxying is globally enabled (default true) a connection assigned to a dead proxy pool is blocked rather than silently falling back to direct egress (#6246); explicit global or per-connection proxy disable is the only sanctioned path to direct egress. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — protects the operator's egress-policy intent (traffic must not leak around a failed proxy); a false positive blocks a healthy connection until proxies are fixed or disabled
entries.test_contract: Negative: dead pool + enabled proxying → connection blocked; proxy_enabled=0 → direct allowed
entries.rollback_or_disable: Disable proxying globally (settings proxyEnabled=false) or per connection

entries.name: field-encryption-aes-256-gcm-at-rest
entries.purpose: Provider credential fields (apiKey, accessToken, refreshToken, idToken) are encrypted at rest as enc:v1:<iv>:<ct>:<tag> using AES-256-GCM with a scryptSync(STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, static salt) key, full 16-byte GCM tag enforced on decrypt (tag-truncation forgery vector closed per :33-38), random IV per value, and auto-migration from the legacy dynamic-salt derivation (v3.7.9 fix; startup migration helper at :375). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: critical — it is the only at-rest protection for every stored provider credential; static-salt KDF and the plaintext-failure fallbacks (CAP-P4-038) are deliberate tradeoffs recorded in its own header
entries.test_contract: Round-trip encrypt/decrypt per field; negative: wrong key → null + credentialDecryptFailed flag; legacy ciphertext auto-migrates on write-back
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unset STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY → passthrough plaintext mode (degradation, not a disable switch); re-encrypt requires key continuity

entries.name: encryption-passthrough-default-and-plaintext-fallbacks
entries.purpose: When STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset (.env.example ships it empty) encryption runs in documented passthrough mode storing plaintext with a console warning, and a cipher failure also falls back to returning plaintext rather than failing closed; the key is searched in data-dir .env, cwd .env, and ~/.hermes/.env when absent from the environment (ensureSecretLoaded). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — a default install stores all provider credentials unencrypted in SQLite; the only signals are log warnings, so operators can believe at-rest encryption exists when it does not
dependencies: operator key provisioning (openssl rand -base64 32 per its own hint)
entries.test_contract: State audit: isEncryptionEnabled() false on keyless install; persistence test asserts stored fields carry enc:v1: prefix only when keyed
entries.rollback_or_disable: Setting the key enables encryption for new writes (existing plaintext rows are not bulk-migrated by this module)

entries.name: jwt-and-apikey-secret-plaintext-persistence
entries.purpose: At boot (ensureSecrets, invoked at instrumentation-node.ts:342) missing JWT_SECRET (48 random bytes base64) and API_KEY_SECRET (32 bytes hex) are generated and persisted via secrets.ts into the key_value table namespace 'secrets' as plain JSON.stringify — NO encryption call — so both signing secrets rest unencrypted in the SQLite file; src/lib/db/AGENTS.md:53 claims secrets.ts is a 'dedicated encrypted store', which the source contradicts. [FACT for source behavior; UPSTREAM-STALE for the doc claim]
entries.risk_class: critical — read access to the OmniRoute SQLite file yields the dashboard-JWT signing key (session forgery) and the API-key HMAC secret, bypassing every management authenticator that trusts them
dependencies: SQLite file permissions as the only protection
env-provided secrets take precedence (persisted values only fill gaps)
entries.test_contract: State audit: query key_value namespace 'secrets' and confirm plaintext JSON values; boot test: env-set secrets are not overwritten
entries.rollback_or_disable: Provide JWT_SECRET/API_KEY_SECRET via env and delete the persisted rows; no encrypted-at-rest variant of this store exists in source

entries.name: api-key-sha256-fast-hash-storage
entries.purpose: Inference API keys are stored/compared as a bare sha256 hex digest — a deliberate per-request performance tradeoff documented at :655-657 (bcrypt/scrypt would add ~100ms per request) with a nosemgrep justification, reasonable for high-entropy random keys but offering no memory-hard defense if keys are weak or short. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — safe while keys are long random strings (the generation path), risky only if user-chosen short keys are permitted; DB read + offline GPU cracking is the attack
entries.test_contract: Audit: minimum key length/entropy at generation; negative: DB digest cannot be reversed by inspection
entries.rollback_or_disable: None (storage format); migration to an HMAC keyed by API_KEY_SECRET would be a source change

entries.name: stale-encryption-key-detection-and-guard
entries.purpose: decryptConnectionFields flags credentialDecryptFailed when a stored enc:v1: value no longer decrypts (changed/unset STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, #6148), logging once per failing row state with a recovery hint (#9927); the models route converts that flag into a 424 with a sanitized message instead of firing an empty-Bearer request that surfaces as a misleading upstream 401. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — an honesty/operability control that prevents misdiagnosis of key loss; it does not recover data, it fails loudly and correctly
entries.test_contract: Negative: key rotated away → 424 naming provider/connection and recovery path; dedupe: one log per row state
entries.rollback_or_disable: Restore the original STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY — rows decrypt again

entries.name: boot-time-secret-strength-validation
entries.purpose: validateSecrets runs during env resolution (runtimeEnv.ts:98) and checks JWT_SECRET (min 32, optional — auto-generated if absent) and API_KEY_SECRET (min 16, required) against length floors and a known-weak-secret denylist (changeme, password, omniroute-default-secret-change-me, etc.). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — catches the worst static misconfigurations at boot, but cannot see auto-generated secrets (those bypass the list by being random) and its denylist is finite
dependencies: runtimeEnv initialization order before secret use
entries.test_contract: Negative: weak/short API_KEY_SECRET → validation failure at boot; absent JWT_SECRET → allowed (auto-gen path)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Provide strong env values; no disable flag found

entries.name: secret-masking-inspector-and-mitm
entries.purpose: A single maskSecret implementation (src/mitm/maskSecrets.ts) — Bearer tokens → '***', sk-/ak-/pk- keys keep first 6 + last 2 chars, opaque ≥40-char tokens keep first 4 + last 2 — redacts credential values from MITM-captured traffic; src/lib/inspector/secretMask.ts:6 re-exports it for the Traffic Inspector (D8: one implementation), and the dashboard pairs it with a SecretMaskToggle component for operator-controlled reveal. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — these are the last line against credential leakage into operator-visible capture surfaces (P7's inspector/MITM lanes); a masking gap exposes whatever secrets traversed the proxy
dependencies: inspector + MITM capture pipelines (agent-surface, cross-ref P7)
entries.test_contract: Unit: known credential shapes masked in captured records; negative: mask toggle defaults to masked
entries.rollback_or_disable: The surfaces themselves are LOCAL_ONLY-gated (routeGuard /api/tools/traffic-inspector/, /api/settings/mitm); disabling capture removes the exposure

entries.name: a2a-rest-dual-authz-posture
entries.purpose: REST A2A task routes (GHSA-jcm5-6wpp-wjj8) accept either a management session or an inference API key, with REQUIRE_API_KEY=true forcing a valid key even when requireLogin=false (alwaysRequireAuth), and key-authenticated callers owner-scoped so other principals' tasks answer as nonexistent; callers must test the failure branch with instanceof Response, not NextResponse, or a 401 silently falls through (its own :29-31 warning). [FACT] Cross-ref P7 (A2A surface).
entries.risk_class: high — an agent-protocol task surface whose local-first default (requireLogin=false + REQUIRE_API_KEY=false) is OPEN by design per its posture matrix; on the HX lane it belongs to the disabled-by-default agent class [AUTHORITY: charter]
entries.test_contract: Posture matrix test over (REQUIRE_API_KEY × requireLogin); owner-scope: key A cannot read key B's tasks; the Response-vs-NextResponse fallthrough regression
entries.rollback_or_disable: requireLogin=true and/or REQUIRE_API_KEY=true closes the open default

entries.name: optional-native-tls-termination
entries.purpose: Native HTTPS is strictly opt-in (#5242): resolveTlsOptions reads OMNIROUTE_TLS_CERT/OMNIROUTE_TLS_KEY file paths and only when BOTH are readable does the standalone server/CLI serve TLS; a missing or half-configured pair logs a warning and falls back to plain HTTP, never crashing. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — the HTTP fallback means a TLS misconfiguration silently downgrades to plaintext serving on the LAN; correct for local-first, but it must be a conscious HX decision where the trust boundary is crossed [AUTHORITY: profile §11]
dependencies: standalone-server-ws.mjs / bin CLI serve command wiring
entries.test_contract: Direct: both vars set → TLS listener; negative: cert without key → HTTP + warning logged
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unset the env vars — plain HTTP (the default)

entries.name: not-established-dedicated-ssrf-named-module
entries.purpose: Searched for src/**/ssrf* and **/*ssrf* implementation files: NONE exist by name; the SSRF capability lives in shared/network/outboundUrlGuard.ts (+Policy) and proxySubscription/fetchGuard.ts instead. [FACT — honest absence recorded so the glob hint is not mistaken for a missed file]
entries.risk_class: low — naming/wayfinding note only; no security content beyond the guards ledgered at CAP-P4-029…033
entries.test_contract: Re-run the filename glob; expect zero *ssrf* files
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a

entries.name: not-established-provider-baseurl-dns-resolution-recheck
entries.purpose: Searched for a fetch-time DNS-resolution re-check on the provider base-url path: the outbound guard validates the URL hostname STRING only (no resolution), while the subscription fetchGuard explicitly re-checks resolution at fetch time (its :22-26 comment); no equivalent re-resolution control was found for provider egress, so a provider hostname that re-resolves to a private/metadata address after validation is not blocked at request time. [INFERENCE from the guard excerpts — the executor fetch layer was not exhaustively read this partition]
entries.risk_class: high — DNS-rebinding/TOCTOU between registration-time validation and request-time connect is the standard SSRF follow-on; only the metadata block (hostname spellings) mitigates it today
dependencies: would require connect-time resolved-IP validation in the executor/fetch layer
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: stand up a hostname that flips A-record post-validation and assert the request is refused — not provable from current source
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a (absence)

entries.name: not-established-storage-encryption-key-rotation
entries.purpose: Searched for STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY rotation tooling: .env.example carries STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY_VERSION=v1 metadata and encryption.ts has legacy-dynamic-salt auto-migration, but no rotate-to-a-NEW-operator-key command, migration, or dual-key decrypt window was found; the documented recovery for a changed key is re-authentication of accounts (RECOVERY_HINT at encryption.ts:76-77). [FACT for the searched scope]
entries.risk_class: medium — key compromise or hygiene rotation currently requires re-entering every credential, which in practice means rotations never happen
dependencies: would need a re-encrypt-all migration with old+new key
entries.test_contract: n/a — absence; if added later: rotation drill on a copy of the DB with decrypt verification
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a (absence)

entries.name: not-established-redirect-target-revalidation
entries.purpose: Searched for redirect (3xx) target re-validation on guarded outbound fetches: the webhook dispatcher validates the initial URL then calls fetch (default redirect:follow) with no visible hook re-checking redirect targets against the guard; the same absence applies to the outbound guard's other consumers. [INFERENCE — the fetch call sites were read, the full redirect behavior of every consumer was not exhaustively traced]
entries.risk_class: medium — a validated public webhook URL that 302s to 169.254.169.254 would reach the metadata service on the second hop under default fetch semantics
dependencies: would require redirect:'manual' + per-hop guard evaluation
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: webhook endpoint issuing a redirect to a blocked target — assert refusal; currently not provable from source
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a (absence)

entries.name: not-established-distributed-login-throttling
entries.purpose: Searched for a shared/persistent login-throttle backend: the login guard is deliberately single-process in-memory (its :4-8 header states it pairs with Cloudflare/reverse-proxy rate limiting and is not a substitute); no DB- or Redis-backed attempt counter and no throttle on the /api/cli/connect password exchange equivalent to loginGuard was found in the guard modules read. [FACT for the guard's scope; INFERENCE for the cli/connect gap]
entries.risk_class: low — acceptable on the single-process standalone deployment HX would run; material only if OmniRoute is ever scaled out
dependencies: deployment-time reverse-proxy limiting (rick's plane, not OmniRoute)
entries.test_contract: n/a — documented design scope, not a defect
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a (absence)
